answer:
Let the two pot radii be \(r_1,r_2\) and heights \(h_1,h_2\). Since each volume is \(200\text{ cm}^3\),

\[
\pi r_i^2 h_i=200
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
h_i=\frac{200}{\pi r_i^2}.
\]

Ignoring the bases, the lateral area of one open cylinder is \(2\pi r_i h_i\), so

\[
L_i=2\pi r_i\frac{200}{\pi r_i^2}=\frac{400}{r_i}.
\]

Thus the total lateral area is

\[
L=400\left(\frac1{r_1}+\frac1{r_2}\right).
\]

The total base area constraint gives

\[
\pi(r_1^2+r_2^2)=100
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
r_1^2+r_2^2=\frac{100}{\pi}.
\]

Minimize \(1/r_1+1/r_2\). Since \(f(x)=x^{-1/2}\) is strictly convex for \(x>0\), Jensen’s inequality gives

\[
\frac1{r_1}+\frac1{r_2}
=
f(r_1^2)+f(r_2^2)
\ge
2f\!\left(\frac{r_1^2+r_2^2}{2}\right).
\]

Equality occurs only when

\[
r_1^2=r_2^2.
\]

Hence the minimum occurs at equal radii:

\[
r_1=r_2=\sqrt{\frac{50}{\pi}}\text{ cm}.
\]

Then each pot has base area \(50\text{ cm}^2\), so

\[
h_i=\frac{200}{50}=4\text{ cm}.
\]

The minimized combined lateral area is

\[
L_{\min}
=2\left(\frac{400}{\sqrt{50/\pi}}\right)
=800\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{50}}
=80\sqrt{2\pi}\text{ cm}^2
\approx 200.53\text{ cm}^2.
\]

Very unequal radii cannot improve this. If one radius is made very small, its height and hence its lateral area \(400/r_i\) become very large; the saving from increasing the other radius is more than offset. Equivalently, strict convexity means any unequal pair gives a strictly larger total lateral area than the equal-radius case.
